# VERIDIAN DPDP — full text

> An independent, third-party DPDP Act compliance record for Indian organisations — "Your DPDP proof, not just your DPDP policy." This is the full text of the public pages of app.veridian-aios.com. The signed-in app on the same host is private and is not described here.

A plain note first: no major search engine has confirmed that it reads llms.txt or llms-full.txt. This file exists so that any assistant or crawler that does can find the right page without guessing. It carries only pages that exist today; there are no guides, articles or documentation pages yet.

## Which edition is for you — https://app.veridian-aios.com/

The DPDP Act asks every organisation for four things. Know what data you hold. Tell people about it. Keep it safe. Prove all three — with a record that outlasts the person who set it up.

- I do this for clients: a CA, CS, audit or legal firm. Your own file is free, always. → https://app.veridian-aios.com/dpdp-firm/
- I do this for us: a company, NGO or firm of our own. → https://app.veridian-aios.com/dpdp-firm/
- Running a school instead? → https://app.veridian-aios.com/dpdp-institution/

## VERIDIAN DPDP for Businesses — https://app.veridian-aios.com/dpdp-firm/

Your DPDP proof — not just your DPDP policy. Built for a company, NGO, trading firm or a CA/CS/audit practice's own file. Compliance due 13 May 2027.

## VERIDIAN DPDP for Schools — https://app.veridian-aios.com/dpdp-institution/

Your DPDP proof — not just a policy nobody reads. Built for a school handling students', parents' and staff's data — most of it belonging to minors. Compliance due 13 May 2027.

## What both edition pages say

### The Schedule to the Act

Ceilings per instance; the Board decides under S.33; no penalty order has been issued in India to date. ₹250 cr S.8(5) security · ₹200 cr S.8(6) breach notice · ₹200 cr S.9 children · ₹150 cr S.10 SDF · ₹50 cr residual · ₹10,000 S.15 individual.

### Everything DPDP, in one place

And the two things the law already requires you to publish are free, forever.

- Where your data actually is: Not "we hold Aadhaar" — the folder, the software, the cupboard. Unknown ones get asked to whoever runs that system.
- A Grievance Officer, published (free, always): Named, appointed properly, on a permanent page. Required by S.8(10).
- Your own public page (free, always): For the 70% of Indian businesses who cannot edit their own website, or have none.
- One email a day, and it is the dashboard: Your people answer yes or no from their inbox. Most never open the website at all.
- An AI Link for any chatbox: Paste it into ChatGPT and let it do the work. It can read, never change. You approve every suggestion.
- Proof that survives people: Dated, unalterable, kept ten years. The IT man leaves; the record does not.
- We never keep your documents: Fingerprints, names and dates. The file stays on your machine. We cannot lose what we never had.
- Deleting somebody, everywhere: Their data is in seven places. We know each one, ask each holder, and prove it afterwards.
- Consent that people actually give: Item by item, on a link. Withdrawing is the same tap as agreeing, because the law says it must be.
- 72 hours, planned in advance: Who is affected, worked out from your data map in minutes rather than weeks.
- Auditors and cyber firms, listed: With what each is actually qualified for. We take no commission from any of them.
- Your vendors, in the same system: Free for them, walled off from each other, and blocked until they sign.

### What we do, and where we stop

Said plainly, because the people selling fear will not.

We do: write down what you hold and where · turn the Act into duties with names and dates · chase them · check the proof · publish your officer and your notices · keep a record nobody can edit · answer people who ask.

We do not: touch your systems · keep your documents · certify you as compliant · give legal advice · quote penalties at you · promise nobody will ever be fined.

### Four ways in

Pricing after a short conversation, because the right number depends on what you hold. No prices are published.

- A company, school or NGO: Run it yourself from day one. Invite a CA later without redoing anything.
- A CA, CS, audit or legal firm: No licence fee, ever. You pay per client file, after you have billed the client. Your own firm's file is free.
- A web agency, payroll bureau or IT firm: Free. Your clients attach you, you sign, you answer what only you know.
- An auditor or cyber firm: Listed on our panel with what you are actually qualified for. We take no commission from you.

### Questions people actually ask

- We run on Gmail. Does that matter? — No. Most Indian companies do. Sign-in is a link to whatever address you use — Gmail, Yahoo or your own domain.
- Has anybody actually been fined? — No. No penalty order has been issued in India to date, and the Board's members are not yet appointed. The date is the real thing, not the fear.
- We are small. Does this apply to us? — Yes. There is no size exemption in the Act. A ten-person firm holding customer phone numbers is a Data Fiduciary.
- Do you touch our systems? — Never. We do not connect to your software, read your files or install anything. We record what you tell us and hold you to it.
- Do you keep our documents? — No. We keep a fingerprint, a name and a date. The document stays with you — which is why you must keep your own originals.
- Can you certify us as compliant? — No, and neither can anyone else. There is no government DPDP certification in India. We document and we record.
- What if we stop paying? — Your proof stays readable and exportable. You lose new entries, not old ones. We do not hold it hostage.
- What happens if you disappear? — Your whole record exports in open formats with the fingerprints intact, and verifies without us. That is the point of building it this way.

### Start with what you hold

One email. No card. Fifteen minutes. Stored in India · no passwords · we never keep your documents.
